methods.description:
Sets the point of the costume the sprite turns around - Scratch's rotation
center. It is also the point that sits at the sprite's position, so it is
where the pen draws from and what `goTo` puts in place.

The point is given in the costume's own pixels, counted from its top left
corner, the same way as [setHitbox(double...)](setHitbox): a sword whose hilt
is 12 pixels from the left and 60 from the top swings around the hilt with
`setRotationCenter(12, 60)`. It grows and shrinks with the sprite's
size and holds for every costume of the sprite. Without it, a sprite turns
around the middle of its costume.

```java
this.addCostume("hand", "assets/clock-hand.png");
this.setRotationCenter(8, 100); // the end of the hand
```
paramDocs: x: the x-coordinate in the costume, from its left edge
y: the y-coordinate in the costume, from its top edge

methods.description:
Sets a `uniform` of the shader: a value the shader reads but the
program decides, such as the time for an animation or a position on the
stage.

The name is the one the shader file declares, `uniform float blocks;`
is set with `set("blocks", 20)`. There is a `set` for one or two
numbers or booleans, a [Vector2](../Vector2/index), a
[Color](../Color/index) (as a `vec3`), and an array of
numbers, `ncoords` at a time, for an array uniform like
`uniform vec3 lights[10];`.
